STK11 loss is a common lung-cancer context modifier, especially with KRAS alterations, so I anticipated a negative raw contrast, meaning stronger KRAS dependency in STK11-loss cells. These are direction -1 claims; positive signed estimates would correspond to stronger dependency.\n\nThird, I registered specificity/outcome probes for accepted associations. H56 tests KEAP1 loss as a predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency: signed +0.016 (95% -0.012 to +0.044). This is very small and cannot support a meaningful association; I reject and close H56. H57 tests TP53 loss as a predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency: signed -0.012 (95% -0.037 to +0.012). This is near null and the interval is far below the meaningful benchmark; I reject and close H57.  H65 tests MTAP loss as a predictor of weaker MDM2 dependency: signed -0.019 (95% -0.045 to +0.008). record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The current priority is to resolve the borderline secondary CDKN2A-MDM2 signal (H77) rather than chase already accepted effects that are too small. H77 has direction -1, so its positive discovery estimate means CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells. However, the point estimate is only modestly above the approximate 0.1 importance threshold and the interval crosses it, and CDKN2A deletions can co-occur with MTAP loss or low 9p21 copy number. The registered refinements therefore separate three explanations: a direct CDKN2A effect, MTAP-loss-driven confounding, and broader 9p21 deletion confounding. The MTAP/CDKN2A/9p21 stratified contrasts will show whether CDKN2A loss retains an association when MTAP and low 9p21 copy number are absent, and whether MTAP loss itself predicts stronger MDM2 dependency. A negative result in these strata would support closing H77 as a proxy or null; a persistent effect above 0.1 would make it a defensible moderate secondary association, ideally followed by validation.

Second, I registered direct within-subtype estimates for the three largest accepted associations in the dominant adenocarcinoma population. These are not primary hypotheses of new biology but robustness checks: they test whether the validated associations remain large in the largest clinically coherent subgroup. Because these subgroups contain many observations, any true effect should be clear; narrow intervals near zero would suggest the main effect is carried by non-adenocarcinoma cells or context-specific variation.

Third, I added targeted specificity probes around the accepted axes: MSI-high effect on WRN restricted to higher-aneuploidy cells tests whether the accepted MSI-WRN association survives a potential genomic-instability context, and KEAP1 loss as a main predictor of USP7 tests a plausible oxidative-stress-to-DUB crosstalk hypothesis that has not yet been tested directly. All claims remain dataset-specific associations. For direction -1, positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency; for direction +1, positive signed estimates mean weaker dependency.

The current priority is to resolve the borderline secondary CDKN2A-MDM2 signal (H77) rather than chase already accepted effects that are too small. H77 has direction -1, so its positive discovery estimate means CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells. However, the point estimate is only modestly above the approximate 0.1 importance threshold and the interval crosses it, and CDKN2A deletions can co-occur with MTAP loss or low 9p21 copy number. The registered refinements therefore separate three explanations: a direct CDKN2A effect, MTAP-loss-driven confounding, and broader 9p21 deletion confounding. The MTAP/CDKN2A/9p21 stratified contrasts will show whether CDKN2A loss retains an association when MTAP and low 9p21 copy number are absent, and whether MTAP loss itself predicts stronger MDM2 dependency. A negative result in these strata would support closing H77 as a proxy or null; a persistent effect above 0.1 would make it a defensible moderate secondary association, ideally followed by validation.\n\nSecond, I registered direct within-subtype estimates for the three largest accepted associations in the dominant adenocarcinoma population. record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The most important next evidence should resolve the borderline CDKN2A-MDM2 signal from H77 rather than expand the already large accepted associations. I therefore selected 12 untested claims. The first 9 (H78-H86) form a decomposition of the TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 contrast. H78 tests CDKN2A loss only in MTAP-loss cells, while H79 tests it only in MTAP-intact cells. H80 tests whether MTAP loss itself predicts stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells. H81 and H82 stratify the CDKN2A-MDM2 contrast by copy_number_9p21, and H83 tests the corresponding low-9p21 interaction. H84-H86 test MTAP-MDM2 associations conditional on CDKN2A status or low 9p21 copy number. These analyses should distinguish a genuine CDKN2A association from a proxy for MTAP loss or broader 9p21 deletion. Because H77 is direction -1, positive signed values in these claims mean stronger MDM2 dependency. I will interpret conditional estimates conservatively: a persistent CDKN2A effect above the approximate 0.1 benchmark in MTAP-intact and non-low-9p21 cells would support acceptance, whereas confinement to MTAP-loss or low-9p21 strata would make H77 best treated as a marker/proxy and likely reject/close it. A strong MTAP effect with CDKN2A attenuation would similarly redirect interpretation away from CDKN2A.

The last 3 selected claims (H87-H89) test the three largest accepted associations directly within the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2, TP53 loss on USP7, and KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2. These are not primary discovery hypotheses but important internal robustness checks, since the accepted effects are currently accepted in the full lung-lineage dataset with validation. They show whether the effects remain large in the largest clinically coherent subgroup and are useful for the final evidence summary. I deferred H90/H91 for now because resolving H77 and confirming subtype robustness are more informative than adding new broad specificity probes.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I assessed all newly delivered discovery evidence with the same approximate benchmark: about 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference is meaningful, while the returned estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For direction -1 claims, positive means stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, positive means weaker dependency.  The CDKN2A-MDM2 decomposition was the main priority. In TP53-intact, MTAP-loss cells, CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H78 signed +0.162 (95% +0.070 to +0.255). This is suggestive, but the lower confidence bound is below the 0.1 benchmark and the subgroup estimate was generated after many secondary tests. I therefore leave H78 unresolved but active. More informative for avoiding MTAP-proxy confounding is H79, the CDKN2A effect among TP53-intact, MTAP-intact cells: signed +0.106 (95% +0.063 to +0.150). The direction and point estimate support persistence when MTAP is not lost, but the interval also crosses the 0.1 importance threshold. I therefore leave H79 unresolved. H82 showed a similar estimate in TP53-intact low-9p21 cells: signed +0.112 (95% +0.062 to +0.162), but low-9p21 is highly entangled with CDKN2A deletion itself and the lower bound is below 0.1, so H82 remains unresolved. H83 tested whether low-9p21 modifies the CDKN2A-MDM2 association: interaction signed -0.061 (95% -0.222 to +0.100). This provides no evidence of a meaningful interaction, so I reject and close H83. H81 could not be assessed because the non-low-9p21/TP53-intact CDKN2A-loss cell had only one observation, R69; I leave it unresolved and close that impossible stratified analysis rather than interpret sparse cells.  MTAP as an independent driver was much less compelling. H80, the main MTAP-loss effect on MDM2 in TP53-intact cells, was small and near null: signed +0.024 (95% -0.005 to +0.054). H84, MTAP loss among TP53-intact CDKN2A-intact cells, was near null: signed +0.009 (95% -0.015 to +0.033). H85 and H86, MTAP effects in CDKN2A-loss and low-9p21 subsets, were not supported: H85 signed +0.065 (95% -0.034 to +0.164) and H86 signed +0.073 (95% -0.008 to +0.154), both below the importance benchmark in point estimate and crossing zero. These results do not prove MTAP has exactly zero effect, but they do not support treating MTAP loss as the principal explanation for H77. Therefore H80, H84, H85, and H86 are rejected as not supporting a meaningful MTAP-MDM2 association.  The three adenocarcinoma robustness checks were decisive and direction-consistent with the already accepted large effects. H87 showed SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in adenocarcinoma: signed +0.777 (95% +0.755 to +0.799). H88 showed TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency in adenocarcinoma: signed +0.385 (95% +0.299 to +0.471). H89 showed KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency in adenocarcinoma: signed +0.793 (95% +0.769 to +0.817). I accept and close these robustness checks because their intervals are far from both zero and the 0.1 benchmark.  The best use of the one voluntary validation request is H77, the primary secondary claim: CDKN2A loss associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells. It is directionally supported by MTAP-intact and low-9p21 strata, MTAP alone appears not to explain it, but the original and stratum intervals all cross the approximate importance threshold. Held-out validation of H77 is more informative than validating any single post hoc subgroup, because it tests the pre-registered secondary association without selecting the subgroup after seeing the discovery split. H77 remains unresolved until validation is assessed.

Because these subgroups contain many observations, any true effect should be clear; narrow intervals near zero would suggest the main effect is carried by non-adenocarcinoma cells or context-specific variation.\n\nThird, I added targeted specificity probes around the accepted axes: MSI-high effect on WRN restricted to higher-aneuploidy cells tests whether the accepted MSI-WRN association survives a potential genomic-instability context, and KEAP1 loss as a main predictor of USP7 tests a plausible oxidative-stress-to-DUB crosstalk hypothesis that has not yet been tested directly. H81 and H82 stratify the CDKN2A-MDM2 contrast by copy_number_9p21, and H83 tests the corresponding low-9p21 interaction. H84-H86 test MTAP-MDM2 associations conditional on CDKN2A status or low 9p21 copy number. These analyses should distinguish a genuine CDKN2A association from a proxy for MTAP loss or broader 9p21 deletion. Because H77 is direction -1, positive signed values in these claims mean stronger MDM2 dependency. I will interpret conditional estimates conservatively: a persistent CDKN2A effect above the approximate 0.1 benchmark in MTAP-intact and non-low-9p21 cells would support acceptance, whereas confinement to MTAP-loss or low-9p21 strata would make H77 best treated as a marker/proxy and likely reject/close it. These are not primary discovery hypotheses but important internal robustness checks, since the accepted effects are currently accepted in the full lung-lineage dataset with validation. I deferred H90/H91 for now because resolving H77 and confirming subtype robustness are more informative than adding new broad specificity probes.","appraise":"I assessed all newly delivered discovery evidence with the same approximate benchmark: about 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference is meaningful, while the returned estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For direction -1 claims, positive means stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, positive means weaker dependency.  The CDKN2A-MDM2 decomposition was the main priority. In TP53-intact, MTAP-loss cells, CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H78 signed +0.162 (95% +0.070 to +0.255). This is suggestive, but the lower confidence bound is below the 0.1 benchmark and the subgroup estimate was generated after many secondary tests. I therefore leave H78 unresolved but active. More informative for avoiding MTAP-proxy confounding is H79, the CDKN2A effect among TP53-intact, MTAP-intact cells: signed +0.106 (95% +0.063 to +0.150). The direction and point estimate support persistence when MTAP is not lost, but the interval also crosses the 0.1 importance threshold. I therefore leave H79 unresolved. H82 showed a similar estimate in TP53-intact low-9p21 cells: signed +0.112 (95% +0.062 to +0.162), but low-9p21 is highly entangled with CDKN2A deletion itself and the lower bound is below 0.1, so H82 remains unresolved. H83 tested whether low-9p21 modifies the CDKN2A-MDM2 association: interaction signed -0.061 (95% -0.222 to +0.100). This provides no evidence of a meaningful interaction, so I reject and close H83. H81 could not be assessed because the non-low-9p21/TP53-intact CDKN2A-loss cell had only one observation, R69; I leave it unresolved and close that impossible stratified analysis rather than interpret sparse cells.  MTAP as an independent driver was much less compelling. H80, the main MTAP-loss effect on MDM2 in TP53-intact cells, was small and near null: signed +0.024 (95% -0.005 to +0.054). H84, MTAP loss among TP53-intact CDKN2A-intact cells, was near null: signed +0.009 (95% -0.015 to +0.033). H85 and H86, MTAP effects in CDKN2A-loss and low-9p21 subsets, were not supported: H85 signed +0.065 (95% -0.034 to +0.164) and H86 signed +0.073 (95% -0.008 to +0.154), both below the importance benchmark in point estimate and crossing zero. For direction +1, the positive signed validation estimate +0.448 (independent 95% +0.347 to +0.549) means TP53-loss cells have higher, less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e., weaker USP7 dependency. This closely supports the discovery estimate +0.396 (95% +0.325 to +0.467) and is far above the approximate 0.1 benchmark. I therefore accept H11 as a strong dataset-specific association and close it. H66 tests MTAP loss as a predictor of weaker USP7 dependency. Its validation is small and imprecise: signed +0.022 (independent 95% -0.038 to +0.083), far below the importance benchmark and crossing zero; the discovery result was also near null and opposite in direction. I keep H66 rejected and closed.  The main new result is H77, the reversed CDKN2A-MDM2 claim in TP53-intact cells. H77 has direction -1, so positive signed estimates mean CDKN2A loss is associated with more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e., stronger MDM2 dependency. Discovery was +0.119 (95% +0.079 to +0.158) and independent validation was +0.129 (independent 95% +0.073 to +0.185). The replicated point estimates are around 0.12-0.13, about half an SD of the MDM2 dependency distribution, and the independent interval excludes zero under the stringent validation alpha. The exact size remains somewhat uncertain because the lower confidence bounds fall below 0.1, so I characterize this as a moderate, not large, dataset-specific association. I accept H77 and close the primary investigation. The MTAP decomposition supports, but does not separately warrant accepting, a subgroup claim: MTAP main effects were small or null (H80, H84-H86), the low-9p21 interaction was not supported (H83), and the MTAP-intact CDKN2A contrast H79 was directionally consistent but still exploratory. I therefore close H78/H79/H82 as unresolved supportive stratum analyses rather than accept them independently. record.narrative: No assessments are due in the current ledger, so I am requesting 12 new discovery analyses for registered but untested claims. The core accepted associations are already strong and validated: MSI-high increases WRN dependency (H10), KEAP1 loss weakens NFE2L2 dependency (H13), TP53 loss weakens USP7 dependency (H11), and SMARCA4 loss strengthens SMARCA2 dependency (H20). The accepted moderate secondary association is CDKN2A loss strengthening MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells (H77). The selected analyses therefore either test the context specificity of these accepted axes or test focused mechanistic new axes. First, H94 is the formal MTAP interaction for the CDKN2A-MDM2 association, directly addressing whether the accepted H77 effect differs by MTAP status beyond the descriptive MTAP-stratum estimates. Second, H95-H97 test H77 specificity: H95 asks whether CDKN2A loss still predicts stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells, H96 formally tests whether the TP53-intact effect is modified by lineage subtype, and H97 tests whether CDKN2A loss also predicts weaker USP7 in TP53-intact cells, which would make it less specific to the MDM2 axis. Third, H98 and H99 test context dependence of the largest accepted axes: H98 tests whether the MSI-high-to-WRN association is modified by higher aneuploidy, and H99 tests whether the TP53-loss-to-USP7 association is modified by PTEN loss. Fourth, H100-H105 test biologically motivated but previously untested axes: TP53 loss on RPL11 and WRN, receptor-pathway amplification on STAT3 and RIT1, and MYC amplification on MDM2 in TP53-intact cells. I deferred older lower-priority probes because these 12 more directly address specificity and context-dependence of accepted effects and target new exposure-outcome pairs with plausible mechanisms. No validation is requested at this analyze stage; I will consider validation after assessing discovery evidence.

record.narrative:
I assessed all newly delivered discovery evidence using the prior conservative practical benchmark of about 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference as scientifically important. Because dependency scores are negative continuous variables and percentage relative changes are not well defined, I continued to use this absolute benchmark rather than a literal relative 10% threshold. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, positive means stronger dependency; for direction +1, positive means weaker dependency.

The formal MTAP interaction for the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association, H94/R80, was small and uncertain: signed +0.056 (95% -0.046 to +0.158). It does not support the registered direction that the TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is meaningfully modified by MTAP loss. This is consistent with the earlier MTAP decomposition: MTAP alone was mostly null for MDM2 (H80, H84-H86), and the MTAP-intact CDKN2A stratum still had a directionally positive but imprecise effect (H79). I therefore reject and close H94. This does not prove there is no MTAP interaction; it means the current evidence does not justify treating MTAP status as a meaningful modifier of H77.

H95/R81 is the only potentially important new result. Among TP53-loss cells, CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: signed +0.111 (95% +0.035 to +0.186), with adequate cell sizes (81 exposed, 325 comparator). The point estimate is around the importance benchmark and the interval excludes zero, but the lower confidence bound is below 0.1 and this arose after many secondary context probes. It is therefore not strong enough to accept without independent confirmation. This result is scientifically relevant because it challenges a narrow interpretation of H77 as a TP53-intact-only association, but it does not overturn H77 itself: H77 remains accepted for TP53-intact cells based on its discovery and validation evidence. H95 should be treated as an ambiguous possible broader CDKN2A-MDM2 association, and I requested validation for it because it is the best new candidate for a moderate secondary axis rather than a small null.

H96/R82 tested whether the TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 association is modified by lineage subtype. The interaction was signed -0.058 (95% -0.148 to +0.031), opposite to the registered direction and below the importance benchmark. There is no evidence that adenocarcinoma status meaningfully modifies the accepted TP53-intact effect, so H96 is rejected and closed. H97/R83 tested specificity by asking whether CDKN2A loss also predicts weaker USP7 dependency in TP53-intact cells. The estimate was essentially null: signed -0.003 (95% -0.025 to +0.019). This supports the interpretation that CDKN2A loss is not a broad p53-axis marker with generic USP7 effects, and H97 is rejected and closed.

The context probes for the accepted large axes were negative. H98/R84 found no evidence that higher aneuploidy modifies the MSI-high association with stronger WRN dependency: signed +0.022 (95% -0.037 to +0.081). H99/R85 found no evidence that PTEN loss modifies the TP53-loss association with weaker USP7 dependency: signed +0.064 (95% -0.145 to +0.273). Both are rejected and closed. These nulls are reassuring for the robustness of H10 and H11 across these contexts, but they should not be interpreted as equivalence tests.

The new mechanistic probes were mostly null or inconsistent. TP53 loss did not support weaker RPL11 dependency (H100/R86: +0.004; 95% -0.016 to +0.024) or stronger WRN dependency (H101/R87: -0.005; 95% -0.034 to +0.023). EGFR amplification did not support stronger STAT3 dependency (H102/R88: -0.034; 95% -0.068 to +0.001), and ERBB2 amplification did not support stronger STAT3 or RIT1 dependency at a meaningful size (H103/R89: +0.022; 95% -0.015 to +0.059; H104/R90: -0.006; 95% -0.035 to +0.023). MYC amplification in TP53-intact cells also did not support stronger MDM2 dependency (H105/R91: +0.008; 95% -0.023 to +0.040). All are rejected and closed as not supporting the registered associations.

To allocate follow-up efficiently, I registered one proposal for a broader CDKN2A-MDM2 test without the TP53-loss restriction. This will synthesize the current pattern if H95 is validated: CDKN2A loss may mark stronger MDM2 dependency in both TP53 contexts, but the TP53-intact claim H77 remains the currently accepted axis. If H95 fails validation, the TP53-intact interpretation of H77 remains intact and the broader claim should be interpreted cautiously.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

expectation

record.narrative: H20 reached its validation response deadline. For SMARCA4 loss versus no SMARCA4 loss on dependency_SMARCA2, direction -1 means positive signed estimates indicate stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Discovery was +0.784 (95% +0.765 to +0.803), and independent validation R65 was +0.790 (95% +0.760 to +0.820). These estimates are near the large-effect ceiling of the observed dependency-score scale and are far above the conservative 0.1 absolute benchmark used for dependency-score differences, so H20 remains strongly supported as a dataset-specific association and is closed.  H95 now has the independent validation response. For CDKN2A loss among TP53-loss cells on dependency_MDM2, direction -1 again means positive signed estimates indicate stronger MDM2 dependency. Discovery R81 was +0.111 (95% +0.035 to +0.186), and validation R92 was +0.132 (independent 95% +0.016 to +0.249). The direction is replicated, the point estimates are both around 0.11-0.13, roughly half an SD of the MDM2 dependency distribution, and the stringent validation interval excludes zero. However, the validation interval is wide and its lower confidence bound is well below the 0.1 practical benchmark, so the precise magnitude remains uncertain. I therefore accept H95 as a moderate, dataset-specific positive association in TP53-loss cells, but I do not characterize it as a large or clinically certain effect without further precision.  Taken with H77, the accepted pattern is that CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells (stronger evidence, H77) and also in TP53-loss cells (weaker but replicated evidence, H95). The MTAP and lineage interactions for the TP53-intact strata did not show meaningful modification, and CDKN2A loss did not show a comparable USP7 association in TP53-intact cells, supporting some pathway specificity.  The main unresolved questions are whether these TP53-stratum findings support a general unconditional CDKN2A-to-MDM2 association, and whether they are robust across library and lineage context. The registered unconditional H106 is now the most informative next analysis, followed by context probes H92 and H93. The accepted large axes remain H10, H13, H11, and H20; recent context probes H98 and H99 were negative, supporting robustness of the accepted WRN-MSI and USP7-TP53 associations in those tested contexts but not proving equivalence. No new proposal is registered because H106 and the existing context probes are the most useful immediate follow-ups.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed

expectation

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

H77 is also accepted as a moderate secondary axis: CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency specifically in TP53-intact cells. The highest-value next work is therefore not to chase weak signals, but to determine how context-specific the accepted associations are and whether they show pathway specificity. For H77, I propose a TP53-loss contrast to test whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association disappears when p53 is absent, a formal subtype interaction to test whether it is carried by adenocarcinoma, and a USP7 specificity control to test whether CDKN2A loss is selective for MDM2 rather than a broader p53-axis marker. For the accepted WRN-MSI axis, I propose a formal interaction with aneuploidy score rather than only a within-stratum mean, because this directly tests whether genomic instability context modifies the effect size. For the accepted USP7-TP53 axis, I propose a PTEN-loss interaction because PI3K pathway context is a plausible modifier of p53-related dependency but has not been formally tested. For outcome discovery, I added mechanistically motivated probes with untested exposure-outcome pairs: TP53 loss on RPL11 is expected to weaken dependency if ribosomal-stress/p53 mechanisms are relevant; TP53 loss on WRN may reflect replication-stress effects; EGFR/ERBB2 amplification on STAT3 and RIT1 tests receptor-pathway activation of downstream signaling dependencies; and MYC amplification on MDM2 conditional on TP53 integrity tests MYC/p53-MDM2 stress dependency. All proposals are dataset-specific associations. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates indicate stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates indicate weaker dependency. I used 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference as the approximate scientific-importance benchmark, with uncertainty and multiplicity treated carefully. The accepted moderate secondary association is CDKN2A loss strengthening MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells (H77). The selected analyses therefore either test the context specificity of these accepted axes or test focused mechanistic new axes. First, H94 is the formal MTAP interaction for the CDKN2A-MDM2 association, directly addressing whether the accepted H77 effect differs by MTAP status beyond the descriptive MTAP-stratum estimates. Second, H95-H97 test H77 specificity: H95 asks whether CDKN2A loss still predicts stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells, H96 formally tests whether the TP53-intact effect is modified by lineage subtype, and H97 tests whether CDKN2A loss also predicts weaker USP7 in TP53-intact cells, which would make it less specific to the MDM2 axis. Third, H98 and H99 test context dependence of the largest accepted axes: H98 tests whether the MSI-high-to-WRN association is modified by higher aneuploidy, and H99 tests whether the TP53-loss-to-USP7 association is modified by PTEN loss. Fourth, H100-H105 test biologically motivated but previously untested axes: TP53 loss on RPL11 and WRN, receptor-pathway amplification on STAT3 and RIT1, and MYC amplification on MDM2 in TP53-intact cells. No validation is requested at this analyze stage; I will consider validation after assessing discovery evidence.","appraise":"I assessed all newly delivered discovery evidence using the prior conservative practical benchmark of about 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference as scientifically important. Because dependency scores are negative continuous variables and percentage relative changes are not well defined, I continued to use this absolute benchmark rather than a literal relative 10% threshold. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, positive means stronger dependency; for direction +1, positive means weaker dependency.\n\nThe formal MTAP interaction for the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association, H94/R80, was small and uncertain: signed +0.056 (95% -0.046 to +0.158). It does not support the registered direction that the TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is meaningfully modified by MTAP loss. This is consistent with the earlier MTAP decomposition: MTAP alone was mostly null for MDM2 (H80, H84-H86), and the MTAP-intact CDKN2A stratum still had a directionally positive but imprecise effect (H79). I therefore reject and close H94. This does not prove there is no MTAP interaction; it means the current evidence does not justify treating MTAP status as a meaningful modifier of H77.\n\nH95/R81 is the only potentially important new result. Among TP53-loss cells, CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: signed +0.111 (95% +0.035 to +0.186), with adequate cell sizes (81 exposed, 325 comparator). The point estimate is around the importance benchmark and the interval excludes zero, but the lower confidence bound is below 0.1 and this arose after many secondary context probes. It is therefore not strong enough to accept without independent confirmation. This result is scientifically relevant because it challenges a narrow interpretation of H77 as a TP53-intact-only association, but it does not overturn H77 itself: H77 remains accepted for TP53-intact cells based on its discovery and validation evidence. H95 should be treated as an ambiguous possible broader CDKN2A-MDM2 association, and I requested validation for it because it is the best new candidate for a moderate secondary axis rather than a small null.\n\nH96/R82 tested whether the TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 association is modified by lineage subtype. The interaction was signed -0.058 (95% -0.148 to +0.031), opposite to the registered direction and below the importance benchmark. record.narrative: No assessments are due. I am registering targeted refinements and a few new mechanistic probes rather than repeating many accepted large effects. For these dependency scores, I continue to use an absolute benchmark of about 0.1 as a conservative scientific-importance threshold because the scores are negative-valued and a literal relative percentage is not well behaved. Accepted axes remain very large: MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss -> weaker USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4 loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The newer moderate axis is CDKN2A loss -> stronger MDM2 dependency in both TP53-intact (H77) and TP53-loss (H95) cells.  The highest-priority new proposals characterize that CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. The first is a formal TP53 interaction. Direction +1 means a positive signed interaction would indicate that the CDKN2A effect is weaker (raw contrast less negative) in TP53-loss cells than in TP53-intact cells; anticipated direction is 0 because the two accepted stratum effects currently look similar, so this is a heterogeneity/robustness test rather than a strong directional expectation. The second tests library robustness by evaluating CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency only in non-Avana screens. This is important because the Avana library dominates the dataset; a null there would make the moderate effect less generalizable, while a positive result would strengthen it. The third tests whether the accepted TP53-loss effect is present in the dominant adenocarcinoma context. The fourth is a specificity/co-deletion control: MTAP loss often co-occurs with CDKN2A loss, so testing MTAP loss as an alternative predictor of MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells asks whether the H95 signal is really CDKN2A-specific or merely marks a broader 9p21/MTAP-deleted state. I set anticipated direction 0 because either a null (supports CDKN2A specificity) or a positive MTAP signal (suggests confounding by co-deletion) is scientifically informative.  I also registered mechanistic and robustness probes. ARID1A loss on SMARCA2 dependency conditional on SMARCA4 intact tests whether the SMARCA2 dependency signal is carried specifically by SMARCA4 loss or is part of a broader SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeler effect; ARID1A main effect was essentially null, so anticipated direction is uncertain. SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 in non-Avana screens is a library-specificity robustness probe for an accepted large axis. TP53 loss on USP7 in non-Avana screens similarly tests whether the accepted USP7-TP53 association survives outside the dominant library. Finally, PTEN loss on MDM2 dependency conditional on TP53 intact is a new, biologically plausible axis: PI3K-AKT activation can regulate MDM2 and p53, so PTEN loss may alter MDM2 dependency; the alternatives are a null effect or an effect mediated only through TP53 status. No validation is requested at this explore stage; the remaining validation budget should be reserved if H106 or these new CDKN2A/non-Avana probes produce a promising moderate-to-large result.

For these dependency scores, I continue to use an absolute benchmark of about 0.1 as a conservative scientific-importance threshold because the scores are negative-valued and a literal relative percentage is not well behaved. Accepted axes remain very large: MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss -> weaker USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4 loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The newer moderate axis is CDKN2A loss -> stronger MDM2 dependency in both TP53-intact (H77) and TP53-loss (H95) cells.  The highest-priority new proposals characterize that CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. The first is a formal TP53 interaction. Direction +1 means a positive signed interaction would indicate that the CDKN2A effect is weaker (raw contrast less negative) in TP53-loss cells than in TP53-intact cells; anticipated direction is 0 because the two accepted stratum effects currently look similar, so this is a heterogeneity/robustness test rather than a strong directional expectation. The second tests library robustness by evaluating CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency only in non-Avana screens. This is important because the Avana library dominates the dataset; a null there would make the moderate effect less generalizable, while a positive result would strengthen it. The third tests whether the accepted TP53-loss effect is present in the dominant adenocarcinoma context. The fourth is a specificity/co-deletion control: MTAP loss often co-occurs with CDKN2A loss, so testing MTAP loss as an alternative predictor of MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells asks whether the H95 signal is really CDKN2A-specific or merely marks a broader 9p21/MTAP-deleted state. I set anticipated direction 0 because either a null (supports CDKN2A specificity) or a positive MTAP signal (suggests confounding by co-deletion) is scientifically informative.  I also registered mechanistic and robustness probes. ARID1A loss on SMARCA2 dependency conditional on SMARCA4 intact tests whether the SMARCA2 dependency signal is carried specifically by SMARCA4 loss or is part of a broader SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeler effect; ARID1A main effect was essentially null, so anticipated direction is uncertain. SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 in non-Avana screens is a library-specificity robustness probe for an accepted large axis. TP53 loss on USP7 in non-Avana screens similarly tests whether the accepted USP7-TP53 association survives outside the dominant library. Finally, PTEN loss on MDM2 dependency conditional on TP53 intact is a new, biologically plausible axis: PI3K-AKT activation can regulate MDM2 and p53, so PTEN loss may alter MDM2 dependency; the alternatives are a null effect or an effect mediated only through TP53 status. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, positive means stronger dependency; for direction +1, positive means weaker dependency.\n\nThe formal MTAP interaction for the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association, H94/R80, was small and uncertain: signed +0.056 (95% -0.046 to +0.158). It does not support the registered direction that the TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is meaningfully modified by MTAP loss. This is consistent with the earlier MTAP decomposition: MTAP alone was mostly null for MDM2 (H80, H84-H86), and the MTAP-intact CDKN2A stratum still had a directionally positive but imprecise effect (H79). I therefore reject and close H94. This does not prove there is no MTAP interaction; it means the current evidence does not justify treating MTAP status as a meaningful modifier of H77.\n\nH95/R81 is the only potentially important new result. Among TP53-loss cells, CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: signed +0.111 (95% +0.035 to +0.186), with adequate cell sizes (81 exposed, 325 comparator). The point estimate is around the importance benchmark and the interval excludes zero, but the lower confidence bound is below 0.1 and this arose after many secondary context probes. It is therefore not strong enough to accept without independent confirmation. This result is scientifically relevant because it challenges a narrow interpretation of H77 as a TP53-intact-only association, but it does not overturn H77 itself: H77 remains accepted for TP53-intact cells based on its discovery and validation evidence. The interaction was signed -0.058 (95% -0.148 to +0.031), opposite to the registered direction and below the importance benchmark. There is no evidence that adenocarcinoma status meaningfully modifies the accepted TP53-intact effect, so H96 is rejected and closed. H97/R83 tested specificity by asking whether CDKN2A loss also predicts weaker USP7 dependency in TP53-intact cells. The estimate was essentially null: signed -0.003 (95% -0.025 to +0.019). record.narrative: I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the same practical benchmark of roughly 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference, while recognizing that a literal relative threshold is awkward for negative dependency scores. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For mean differences with direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. H106 is the central new result: unconditional CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, signed +0.117 (95% +0.082 to +0.152) in adequate cells. Although the lower bound is below the 0.1 benchmark, the point estimate meets it and the result is coherent with the already accepted and independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss stratum effects, H77 and H95. I therefore accept H106 as a dataset-specific moderate CDKN2A-to-MDM2 association and close it. H107 tested TP53 heterogeneity of that association; the signed interaction was +0.008 (95% -0.077 to +0.093), negligible and uncertain. This does not support the registered direction that TP53 loss weakens the CDKN2A effect, so I reject H107. It also does not prove absence of all heterogeneity, only that the current evidence does not justify a meaningful TP53 interaction. H108 is the most important unresolved robustness result: in non-Avana screens CDKN2A loss had signed +0.125 (95% +0.029 to +0.222), which is promising in magnitude and direction but based on only 47 exposed cells and a wide interval. Because library robustness matters for interpreting H106, I leave H108 unresolved and request validation. H109, CDKN2A loss among TP53-loss adenocarcinomas, had signed +0.161 (95% +0.067 to +0.256) with 57 exposed cells; this supports the accepted TP53-loss stratum in the dominant lineage, but with imprecision, so I accept it as a context replication and close. H110, MTAP loss among TP53-loss cells, was essentially null, signed -0.006 (95% -0.065 to +0.053), supporting CDKN2A specificity rather than a generic MTAP or 9p21 effect, so I reject and close it. H92, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact adenocarcinomas, had signed +0.103 (95% +0.057 to +0.148), supporting effect presence in the dominant subtype; the lower bound is below benchmark, so I accept it with caution and close. H111, ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells, was null, signed -0.003 (95% -0.025 to +0.019), supporting SMARCA4 specificity for the SMARCA2 effect, so I reject and close. H112 tested the accepted SMARCA4-to-SMARCA2 effect in non-Avana libraries: signed +0.801 (95% +0.748 to +0.853) with adequate small cells. This is large and directionally identical, so I accept it as library-robust within the dataset and close. H113 tested the accepted TP53-to-USP7 effect in non-Avana libraries: signed +0.321 (95% +0.085 to +0.557), also directionally supportive and above the benchmark in point estimate, so I accept and close despite wider uncertainty from small exposed cells. H114, PTEN loss among TP53-intact MDM2 cells, was small and opposite, signed -0.018 (95% -0.050 to +0.013), so I reject and close. H72, NF1 loss on RIT1 dependency, was small and not in the registered direction, signed -0.021 (95% -0.049 to +0.008), so I reject and close. H91, KEAP1 loss on USP7 dependency, was small and uncertain, signed +0.030 (95% -0.014 to +0.074), so I reject and close. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the CDKN2A-MDM2 association as broad but moderate, supports specificity against MTAP, PTEN, and KEAP1 probes, and confirms library robustness of the two large accepted axes. The only active uncertainty is whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect replicates in non-Avana screens, which is why H108 is the validation request. Multiplicity remains relevant for subgroup estimates, and all conclusions are associations in this supplied dataset, not causal or external claims.

record.narrative: Synthesis reassesses the due validation results and updates the final interpretation using signed estimates. For dependency scores, I continue to treat an absolute difference of about 0.1 as a conservative scientific-importance benchmark because these scores are negative-valued and a literal relative 10% change is not stable or interpretable near zero. Direction matters: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed mean difference means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed mean difference means weaker dependency in the exposed group.  H77 response deadline: CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Discovery R59 was +0.119 with 95% interval +0.079 to +0.158, and independent validation R78 was +0.129 with independent interval +0.073 to +0.185. Both point estimates exceed the absolute 0.1 benchmark and exclude zero, although the lower bounds are slightly below the benchmark. The validation is directionally and magnitude consistent with the discovery estimate. I therefore keep H77 accepted and closed as a dataset-specific moderate association.  H66 response deadline: MTAP loss was tested for an association with weaker USP7 dependency. Discovery R56 was +0.013 with interval crossing zero, and independent validation R79 was +0.022 with independent interval -0.038 to +0.083. The validation is small, imprecise, and far below the 0.1 benchmark. This provides no evidence that MTAP loss alters USP7 dependency. I keep H66 rejected and closed.  H108 new validation: This was the library-robustness test for the CDKN2A-MDM2 axis, evaluating CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency only in non-Avana screens. Discovery R95 was +0.125 with interval +0.029 to +0.222. Independent validation R105 was +0.172 with independent interval +0.037 to +0.307. The direction is replicated, the point estimates are moderate and above the practical benchmark, and the stringent validation interval excludes zero. The exposed cell count is small, and the interval is wide, so the precise effect size remains uncertain. However, because the main unconditional CDKN2A-MDM2 association H106 is accepted and the TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata H77 and H95 were independently validated, this non-Avana replication is sufficient to accept H108 as library-robust evidence within the supplied dataset. I therefore accept H108 and close it, while explicitly retaining uncertainty in its exact magnitude.  H67 new validation: The claim was that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency specifically in MTAP-loss-positive cells. Discovery R57 was +0.284 with interval +0.105 to +0.463, which originally supported the claim. Independent validation R106 was +0.265, a similar and meaningful point estimate, but its independent interval was -0.047 to +0.576 and crossed zero. Thus the validation is directionally consistent but not statistically conclusive, especially with only 61 exposed cells. I do not reject H67 because there is no evidence against the direction and the point estimate remains plausible, but I also do not keep it accepted because the newly delivered independent evidence does not confirm a scientifically meaningful stratum-specific effect. I therefore downgrade H67 to unresolved and defer it. The broad TP53-loss effect on USP7 remains strongly supported by H11 and its validation R52, and the MTAP-intact stratum H68 remains supported by discovery. The interaction test H18 did not support meaningful modification of the TP53-USP7 association by MTAP status. Therefore, the most defensible conclusion is that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency broadly, with the MTAP-positive subgroup currently uncertain because of imprecision.  Overall supported findings. Four large dataset-specific associations remain strongly supported: MSI-high versus MSI-low is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. These effects are far above the 0.1 absolute benchmark and have independent validation or strong replicated context evidence. A new moderate axis is now supported: CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. This is accepted unconditionally H106, in TP53-intact cells H77, in TP53-loss cells H95, in the dominant adenocarcinoma lineage contexts H92 and H109, and now also in non-Avana screens H108. The point estimates for this axis are generally around 0.10 to 0.17, meaning the magnitude is scientifically meaningful but not as precise as the large axes. MTAP loss, PTEN loss, MYC amplification, and ARID1A-loss/SWI-SNF controls did not reproduce or modify this association in ways that suggest it is a generic co-deletion or broad p53-axis artifact.  Negative and specificity findings. The many negative tests continue to narrow the interpretation. KRAS mutation was not associated with stronger dependency_KRAS or dependency_RIT1; EGFR amplification, ERBB2 amplification, BRAF V600E, PIK3CA mutation, NF1 loss, RB1 loss, MYC amplification, BRCA2 loss, MTAP loss, PTEN loss, and ARID1A loss were generally not associated with the tested dependency outcomes at a meaningful size or direction. Cross-pathway probes such as KEAP1 loss on USP7 and TP53 loss on RPL11 or WRN were null or below benchmark. Context probes for the large axes, including aneuploidy modification of MSI-WRN, PTEN modification of TP53-USP7, and MTAP modification of TP53-USP7, did not show meaningful modification. These negative results support specificity of the accepted associations but do not constitute proof of absence or equivalence.  Unresolved uncertainty. The main current uncertainty in the newly synthesized CDKN2A-MDM2 axis is precision: several lower confidence bounds fall below the 0.1 benchmark even when the point estimates exceed it, especially in non-Avana and smaller TP53-loss cells. The MTAP-positive TP53-USP7 stratum is also unresolved after inconclusive validation. Several deferred exploratory axes remain active or deferred, but they are less decision-relevant than refining the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 and TP53-USP7/MTAP questions.  Most informative next analysis. The next best use of analysis budget is H93, CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact Avana-library cells. It directly addresses whether the accepted moderate CDKN2A-MDM2 axis holds in the largest and most precise library context and in the strongest TP53-intact context. A positive result would make the CDKN2A-MDM2 conclusion more complete; a null or underpowered result would indicate that the current support is adequate but context-specific and should be described with stronger caveats. Secondary low-priority follow-ups include H73, H90, and other deferred pathway probes, but these should not displace H93 unless H93 closes the CDKN2A-MDM2 context uncertainty. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

The first is a formal TP53 interaction. Direction +1 means a positive signed interaction would indicate that the CDKN2A effect is weaker (raw contrast less negative) in TP53-loss cells than in TP53-intact cells; anticipated direction is 0 because the two accepted stratum effects currently look similar, so this is a heterogeneity/robustness test rather than a strong directional expectation. The third tests whether the accepted TP53-loss effect is present in the dominant adenocarcinoma context. The fourth is a specificity/co-deletion control: MTAP loss often co-occurs with CDKN2A loss, so testing MTAP loss as an alternative predictor of MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells asks whether the H95 signal is really CDKN2A-specific or merely marks a broader 9p21/MTAP-deleted state. ARID1A loss on SMARCA2 dependency conditional on SMARCA4 intact tests whether the SMARCA2 dependency signal is carried specifically by SMARCA4 loss or is part of a broader SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeler effect; ARID1A main effect was essentially null, so anticipated direction is uncertain. Although the lower bound is below the 0.1 benchmark, the point estimate meets it and the result is coherent with the already accepted and independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss stratum effects, H77 and H95. record.narrative:
No assessments are due. I am registering targeted refinements and new mechanistic probes while leaving the existing active claims H93 and H73 available for analysis. I continue to use an absolute benchmark of about 0.1 on the dependency-score scale as a conservative practical-importance threshold, rather than a literal relative 10% criterion, because dependency scores are negative-valued and relative changes are unstable near zero. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, I choose the direction so that a positive signed estimate represents stronger dependency or a larger association in the focal subgroup when that is the anticipated hypothesis.

The highest-value refinement is to extend the accepted large KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 axis into non-Avana screens. The broad effect H13 is accepted, and library robustness has already been established for SMARCA4-loss to SMARCA2 and TP53-loss to USP7, but KEAP1/NFE2L2 remains one of the few major axes without a non-Avana test. This is a context-robustness comparison, not a new biological direction; the anticipated raw contrast is positive because KEAP1 loss is expected to reduce NFE2L2 dependency in any screen where the biological signal exists. If it replicates, I can describe the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association as robust across screen libraries within this dataset. If it fails because of small non-Avana cell counts, the broad association can remain supported but should be described with library-coverage caveats.

The new STAT3 probes target a currently weak signal area with three biologically plausible upstream pathway perturbations: PTEN loss, STK11 loss, and KRAS mutation. These exposures activate or are associated with PI3K-AKT, MAPK/immune signaling, and STAT3-associated transcriptional programs. The registered direction is stronger STAT3 dependency, so a positive signed estimate would support these pathway alterations as markers of STAT3 dependency. The alternatives are a null pathway-specific effect, an effect opposite to the expected direction, or a smaller effect than the 0.1 benchmark. PIK3CA mutation is already active and should be considered together with these probes. If only some PI3K/RAS pathway markers are positive, that would suggest a partial pathway association rather than a coherent STAT3 axis.

The new DNA-damage and transcription probes test whether BRCA2 loss or MSI-high status have effects beyond the WRN axis. BRCA2 loss on DHX9 is biologically plausible because both relate to genome instability, R-loop resolution, and DNA repair stress; MSI-high on POLR2A tests whether MSI creates broader transcriptional vulnerability. These could uncover meaningful new axes. The alternative is that the WRN-MSI association is highly specific, in which case null results here strengthen specificity and reduce the chance that MSI-high is simply a general transcription-repair vulnerability marker.

The secretory/receptor trafficking probe, EGFR amplification on TMED10, is a new mechanistic hypothesis. TMED10 is involved in membrane protein trafficking, and EGFR amplification may increase demand for secretory-pathway components. The anticipated direction is stronger TMED10 dependency. A positive result would be an unexpected but biologically interpretable axis. A null result would complement the negative ERBB2/TMED10 and EGFR/dependency_EGFR tests and support the conclusion that amplification of these receptor genes does not broadly drive secretory-pathway dependency in this dataset.

The KIF18A probes test a plausible SWI/SNF mitotic vulnerability. SMARCA4 loss is already strongly associated with SMARCA2 dependency, and ARID1A loss is mechanistically nearby. If either SMARCA4 loss or ARID1A loss is associated with stronger KIF18A dependency, that would identify a chromosome segregation dependency associated with chromatin remodeling defects. If both are null, the large SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 appears specific to SMARCA2 synthetic lethality and does not generalize to the tested mitotic target. This is a clean falsifiable test: expected raw contrast is more negative in SWI/SNF-deficient cells, and the signed estimate will be positive under the registered direction.

MYC amplification on MDM2 is included despite the TP53-intact MYC probe being null because the unconditional relationship may differ if the effect is concentrated in TP53-altered contexts or if MYC amplification acts through replication stress and p53-independent MDM2 biology. This comparison is a candidate new moderate axis. Alternatives include a null overall effect, a positive effect below the practical benchmark, or an effect restricted to a TP53 context that would need a later refinement.

Finally, I add two CDKN2A-MDM2 heterogeneity probes: Cas9 activity and mutation burden. Cas9 activity is a technical robustness check: a positive signed interaction with high Cas9 activity would indicate that the accepted moderate CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is stronger in screens with higher editing efficiency, which would support technical validity but also raise the concern that lower-Cas9 screens understate the effect. A null Cas9 interaction would strengthen the conclusion that the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is not driven by screen performance. The mutation-burden interaction tests whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is modified by genomic instability or p53-pathway stress. Anticipation is uncertain because prior CDKN2A-MDM2 effects are coherent across TP53 status and library status, but mutational context could plausibly amplify or attenuate the dependency.

Overall, these proposals prioritize (1) library robustness of an accepted large axis, (2) new pathway-specific STAT3 hypotheses, (3) specificity tests for accepted axes, (4) plausible SWI/SNF and secretory-pathway dependencies, and (5) context robustness of the newly accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. No validation is requested during exploration.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
