I continue to use an absolute benchmark of about 0.1 on the dependency-score scale as a conservative practical-importance threshold, rather than a literal relative 10% criterion, because dependency scores are negative-valued and relative changes are unstable near zero. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, I choose the direction so that a positive signed estimate represents stronger dependency or a larger association in the focal subgroup when that is the anticipated hypothesis.\n\nThe highest-value refinement is to extend the accepted large KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 axis into non-Avana screens. The broad effect H13 is accepted, and library robustness has already been established for SMARCA4-loss to SMARCA2 and TP53-loss to USP7, but KEAP1/NFE2L2 remains one of the few major axes without a non-Avana test. This is a context-robustness comparison, not a new biological direction; the anticipated raw contrast is positive because KEAP1 loss is expected to reduce NFE2L2 dependency in any screen where the biological signal exists. If it replicates, I can describe the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association as robust across screen libraries within this dataset. If it fails because of small non-Avana cell counts, the broad association can remain supported but should be described with library-coverage caveats.\n\nThe new STAT3 probes target a currently weak signal area with three biologically plausible upstream pathway perturbations: PTEN loss, STK11 loss, and KRAS mutation. These exposures activate or are associated with PI3K-AKT, MAPK/immune signaling, and STAT3-associated transcriptional programs. The registered direction is stronger STAT3 dependency, so a positive signed estimate would support these pathway alterations as markers of STAT3 dependency. The alternatives are a null pathway-specific effect, an effect opposite to the expected direction, or a smaller effect than the 0.1 benchmark. PIK3CA mutation is already active and should be considered together with these probes. If only some PI3K/RAS pathway markers are positive, that would suggest a partial pathway association rather than a coherent STAT3 axis.\n\nThe new DNA-damage and transcription probes test whether BRCA2 loss or MSI-high status have effects beyond the WRN axis. BRCA2 loss on DHX9 is biologically plausible because both relate to genome instability, R-loop resolution, and DNA repair stress; MSI-high on POLR2A tests whether MSI creates broader transcriptional vulnerability. These could uncover meaningful new axes. The alternative is that the WRN-MSI association is highly specific, in which case null results here strengthen specificity and reduce the chance that MSI-high is simply a general transcription-repair vulnerability marker.\n\nThe secretory/receptor trafficking probe, EGFR amplification on TMED10, is a new mechanistic hypothesis. TMED10 is involved in membrane protein trafficking, and EGFR amplification may increase demand for secretory-pathway components. The anticipated direction is stronger TMED10 dependency. A positive result would be an unexpected but biologically interpretable axis. A null result would complement the negative ERBB2/TMED10 and EGFR/dependency_EGFR tests and support the conclusion that amplification of these receptor genes does not broadly drive secretory-pathway dependency in this dataset.\n\nThe KIF18A probes test a plausible SWI/SNF mitotic vulnerability. SMARCA4 loss is already strongly associated with SMARCA2 dependency, and ARID1A loss is mechanistically nearby. If either SMARCA4 loss or ARID1A loss is associated with stronger KIF18A dependency, that would identify a chromosome segregation dependency associated with chromatin remodeling defects. If both are null, the large SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 appears specific to SMARCA2 synthetic lethality and does not generalize to the tested mitotic target. This is a clean falsifiable test: expected raw contrast is more negative in SWI/SNF-deficient cells, and the signed estimate will be positive under the registered direction.\n\nMYC amplification on MDM2 is included despite the TP53-intact MYC probe being null because the unconditional relationship may differ if the effect is concentrated in TP53-altered contexts or if MYC amplification acts through replication stress and p53-independent MDM2 biology. This comparison is a candidate new moderate axis. Alternatives include a null overall effect, a positive effect below the practical benchmark, or an effect restricted to a TP53 context that would need a later refinement.\n\nFinally, I add two CDKN2A-MDM2 heterogeneity probes: Cas9 activity and mutation burden. Cas9 activity is a technical robustness check: a positive signed interaction with high Cas9 activity would indicate that the accepted moderate CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is stronger in screens with higher editing efficiency, which would support technical validity but also raise the concern that lower-Cas9 screens understate the effect. A null Cas9 interaction would strengthen the conclusion that the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is not driven by screen performance. The mutation-burden interaction tests whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is modified by genomic instability or p53-pathway stress. Anticipation is uncertain because prior CDKN2A-MDM2 effects are coherent across TP53 status and library status, but mutational context could plausibly amplify or attenuate the dependency.\n\nOverall, these proposals prioritize (1) library robustness of an accepted large axis, (2) new pathway-specific STAT3 hypotheses, (3) specificity tests for accepted axes, (4) plausible SWI/SNF and secretory-pathway dependencies, and (5) context robustness of the newly accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. I am not requesting validation at this analyze stage; validation will be considered after assessing these discovery results, preferably only for a new result strong enough to alter the accepted axis set or clarify the CDKN2A-MDM2 conclusion.","appraise":"I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the same practical benchmark of roughly 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference, while recognizing that a literal relative threshold is awkward for negative dependency scores. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. H106 is the central new result: unconditional CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, signed +0.117 (95% +0.082 to +0.152) in adequate cells. Although the lower bound is below the 0.1 benchmark, the point estimate meets it and the result is coherent with the already accepted and independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss stratum effects, H77 and H95. I therefore accept H106 as a dataset-specific moderate CDKN2A-to-MDM2 association and close it. H107 tested TP53 heterogeneity of that association; the signed interaction was +0.008 (95% -0.077 to +0.093), negligible and uncertain. This does not support the registered direction that TP53 loss weakens the CDKN2A effect, so I reject H107. It also does not prove absence of all heterogeneity, only that the current evidence does not justify a meaningful TP53 interaction. H108 is the most important unresolved robustness result: in non-Avana screens CDKN2A loss had signed +0.125 (95% +0.029 to +0.222), which is promising in magnitude and direction but based on only 47 exposed cells and a wide interval. Because library robustness matters for interpreting H106, I leave H108 unresolved and request validation. H109, CDKN2A loss among TP53-loss adenocarcinomas, had signed +0.161 (95% +0.067 to +0.256) with 57 exposed cells; this supports the accepted TP53-loss stratum in the dominant lineage, but with imprecision, so I accept it as a context replication and close. H110, MTAP loss among TP53-loss cells, was essentially null, signed -0.006 (95% -0.065 to +0.053), supporting CDKN2A specificity rather than a generic MTAP or 9p21 effect, so I reject and close it. H92, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact adenocarcinomas, had signed +0.103 (95% +0.057 to +0.148), supporting effect presence in the dominant subtype; the lower bound is below benchmark, so I accept it with caution and close. H111, ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells, was null, signed -0.003 (95% -0.025 to +0.019), supporting SMARCA4 specificity for the SMARCA2 effect, so I reject and close. H112 tested the accepted SMARCA4-to-SMARCA2 effect in non-Avana libraries: signed +0.801 (95% +0.748 to +0.853) with adequate small cells. This is large and directionally identical, so I accept it as library-robust within the dataset and close. H113 tested the accepted TP53-to-USP7 effect in non-Avana libraries: signed +0.321 (95% +0.085 to +0.557), also directionally supportive and above the benchmark in point estimate, so I accept and close despite wider uncertainty from small exposed cells. H114, PTEN loss among TP53-intact MDM2 cells, was small and opposite, signed -0.018 (95% -0.050 to +0.013), so I reject and close. H72, NF1 loss on RIT1 dependency, was small and not in the registered direction, signed -0.021 (95% -0.049 to +0.008), so I reject and close. H91, KEAP1 loss on USP7 dependency, was small and uncertain, signed +0.030 (95% -0.014 to +0.074), so I reject and close. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the CDKN2A-MDM2 association as broad but moderate, supports specificity against MTAP, PTEN, and KEAP1 probes, and confirms library robustness of the two large accepted axes. Discovery R95 was +0.125 with interval +0.029 to +0.222. Independent validation R105 was +0.172 with independent interval +0.037 to +0.307. The direction is replicated, the point estimates are moderate and above the practical benchmark, and the stringent validation interval excludes zero. The exposed cell count is small, and the interval is wide, so the precise effect size remains uncertain. However, because the main unconditional CDKN2A-MDM2 association H106 is accepted and the TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata H77 and H95 were independently validated, this non-Avana replication is sufficient to accept H108 as library-robust evidence within the supplied dataset. I therefore accept H108 and close it, while explicitly retaining uncertainty in its exact magnitude.  H67 new validation: The claim was that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency specifically in MTAP-loss-positive cells. Discovery R57 was +0.284 with interval +0.105 to +0.463, which originally supported the claim. Independent validation R106 was +0.265, a similar and meaningful point estimate, but its independent interval was -0.047 to +0.576 and crossed zero. Thus the validation is directionally consistent but not statistically conclusive, especially with only 61 exposed cells. I do not reject H67 because there is no evidence against the direction and the point estimate remains plausible, but I also do not keep it accepted because the newly delivered independent evidence does not confirm a scientifically meaningful stratum-specific effect. I therefore downgrade H67 to unresolved and defer it. The broad TP53-loss effect on USP7 remains strongly supported by H11 and its validation R52, and the MTAP-intact stratum H68 remains supported by discovery. The interaction test H18 did not support meaningful modification of the TP53-USP7 association by MTAP status. Therefore, the most defensible conclusion is that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency broadly, with the MTAP-positive subgroup currently uncertain because of imprecision.  Overall supported findings. Four large dataset-specific associations remain strongly supported: MSI-high versus MSI-low is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. These effects are far above the 0.1 absolute benchmark and have independent validation or strong replicated context evidence. A new moderate axis is now supported: CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. This is accepted unconditionally H106, in TP53-intact cells H77, in TP53-loss cells H95, in the dominant adenocarcinoma lineage contexts H92 and H109, and now also in non-Avana screens H108. The point estimates for this axis are generally around 0.10 to 0.17, meaning the magnitude is scientifically meaningful but not as precise as the large axes. MTAP loss, PTEN loss, MYC amplification, and ARID1A-loss/SWI-SNF controls did not reproduce or modify this association in ways that suggest it is a generic co-deletion or broad p53-axis artifact.  Negative and specificity findings. The many negative tests continue to narrow the interpretation. KRAS mutation was not associated with stronger dependency_KRAS or dependency_RIT1; EGFR amplification, ERBB2 amplification, BRAF V600E, PIK3CA mutation, NF1 loss, RB1 loss, MYC amplification, BRCA2 loss, MTAP loss, PTEN loss, and ARID1A loss were generally not associated with the tested dependency outcomes at a meaningful size or direction. Cross-pathway probes such as KEAP1 loss on USP7 and TP53 loss on RPL11 or WRN were null or below benchmark. Context probes for the large axes, including aneuploidy modification of MSI-WRN, PTEN modification of TP53-USP7, and MTAP modification of TP53-USP7, did not show meaningful modification. These negative results support specificity of the accepted associations but do not constitute proof of absence or equivalence.  Unresolved uncertainty. The main current uncertainty in the newly synthesized CDKN2A-MDM2 axis is precision: several lower confidence bounds fall below the 0.1 benchmark even when the point estimates exceed it, especially in non-Avana and smaller TP53-loss cells. The MTAP-positive TP53-USP7 stratum is also unresolved after inconclusive validation. Several deferred exploratory axes remain active or deferred, but they are less decision-relevant than refining the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 and TP53-USP7/MTAP questions.  Most informative next analysis. The next best use of analysis budget is H93, CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact Avana-library cells. It directly addresses whether the accepted moderate CDKN2A-MDM2 axis holds in the largest and most precise library context and in the strongest TP53-intact context. A positive result would make the CDKN2A-MDM2 conclusion more complete; a null or underpowered result would indicate that the current support is adequate but context-specific and should be described with stronger caveats. Secondary low-priority follow-ups include H73, H90, and other deferred pathway probes, but these should not displace H93 unless H93 closes the CDKN2A-MDM2 context uncertainty. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability."}}

record.narrative: I assessed all newly delivered discovery estimates using the same signed-estimate convention and the practical absolute benchmark of about 0.1 on the dependency-score scale. Dependency scores are negative-valued, so a literal relative 10% change is unstable near zero; the 0.1 benchmark is therefore used as a conservative scientific-importance threshold rather than a causal claim. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate represents a larger focal-subgroup association when the hypothesis was registered that way. H93 tested CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact Avana-library cells. The signed estimate was +0.117, 95% CI +0.074 to +0.160, with adequate cell sizes (281 exposed, 1121 comparator). The lower bound is slightly below the 0.1 benchmark, but the point estimate is above it and the result is highly coherent with the already accepted broad CDKN2A-MDM2 association and with independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata. I therefore accept H93 as a context-complete replication in the dominant TP53-intact Avana stratum and close it. H115 tested the accepted KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 association in non-Avana screens. The signed estimate was +0.794, 95% CI +0.746 to +0.842, with 40 exposed and 195 comparator cells. Although exposed cells are modest, the effect is enormous, far above the benchmark, and directionally identical to the broad validated effect. I accept it with a small-cell precision caveat and close it, supporting library robustness of this major axis within this dataset. H90 tested whether MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency in cells with aneuploidy above the median. The signed estimate was +0.801, 95% CI +0.761 to +0.841, with 65 exposed cells. This is a large, directionally supportive context replication, so I accept and close H90. H116 is the most important new discovery: PTEN loss was associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.267, 95% CI +0.215 to +0.319, with 266 exposed cells. This is far above the practical benchmark and biologically plausible through PI3K/PTEN-related signaling pathways. However, it is a single new-axis discovery among several STAT3 probes, the estimate is unadjusted for co-occurring molecular alterations, and independent confirmation is not yet available. I therefore record H116 as unresolved but active and request independent validation rather than prematurely accepting it as a new supported axis. The remaining STAT3 probes did not support a coherent broader PI3K/RAS pathway effect: H117 STK11 loss was +0.015, CI -0.014 to +0.043; H118 KRAS mutation was -0.018, CI -0.042 to +0.007; H73 PIK3CA mutation was -0.014, CI -0.041 to +0.014. All are small, uncertain, and far below the benchmark, so I reject and close them. H125 tested Cas9-activity modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction. The signed interaction was +0.048, 95% CI -0.027 to +0.123. It does not support a meaningful high-Cas9 interaction, but the upper bound crosses the practical benchmark and the cell counts, while adequate, are not large. I keep H125 unresolved and deferred rather than rejecting it as proof of absence. H126 tested mutation-burden modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction and was essentially null, -0.001, CI -0.069 to +0.068, entirely below the benchmark; I reject and close it. H119 tested BRCA2 loss on DHX9 dependency and found a small null effect, +0.012, CI -0.020 to +0.044. H120 tested MSI-high on POLR2A dependency and found a small opposite/null effect, -0.004, CI -0.035 to +0.028. H122 tested SMARCA4 loss on KIF18A dependency and found a small opposite/null effect, -0.007, CI -0.026 to +0.013. All are below the benchmark and do not support new axes; I reject and close them. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the accepted large axes: MSI-high-WRN remains strong in high-aneuploidy cells, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency is library-robust, and the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is now replicated in the largest TP53-intact Avana context. It also identifies a potentially major new PTEN-loss to stronger STAT3 dependency association, but I hold final acceptance pending independent validation. Multiplicity remains relevant for new subgroup or subgroup-marker claims, and all current conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset rather than causal or externally generalizable effects.
